title: Quasi-coherent termwise models on quasi-compact separated schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] which is separated, meaning that its structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ has closed-immersion diagonal [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], there exist an integer-indexed cochain complex $F^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with each $F^i$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and an isomorphism $Q(F^\bullet)\simeq K$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, where $Q$ is the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No boundedness assumption is imposed on $K$ or $F^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 08DB, perfect-proposition-quasi-compact-affine-diagonal, essential surjectivity specialized to a separated scheme; this specialization is used explicitly in Tag 0BQR, perfect-lemma-nonzero-some-cohomology, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: For every scheme $T$ let $\mathcal A_T$ be the full category of quasi-coherent modules. The kernel, cokernel/image, and binary-sum nodes give closure under the corresponding ambient constructions; zero is the associated zero module. Thus the ambient coimage-to-image isomorphism belongs to this full subcategory, which is abelian with the same kernels and cokernels. Its inclusion is exact. Cohomology of a complex in $\mathcal A_T$ is computed using those same kernels and cokernels, hence is quasi-coherent. The exact-functor factorization therefore gives $I_T:D(\mathcal A_T)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ and identifies $I_T(Q_{\mathcal A_T}F)$ with the localization of the underlying sheaf complex.

source.place: Section 01LA, item (5), with 01IC and 01ID; induced functor of perfect.tex equation 08DC.

proof.text: The diagonal of $X$ is a closed immersion. By the affine-local description of closed immersions its inverse image over any affine open of $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ is a spectrum of a quotient ring, hence quasi-compact by the spectrum compactness node. The diagonal is therefore quasi-compact, so $X$ is quasi-separated. For any affine open $U\subseteq X$, the inclusion $j:U\to X$ is affine by the affine-source/separated-target lemma. This uses the given absolute separatedness; no finite-type, field, or Noetherian hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Tag 01SG (lemma-affine-permanence), applied as in perfect.tex Tag 08DB; closed-immersion description: Tag 01QO.

proof.text: For this affine $j$, the affine higher-direct-image node gives quasi-coherence of $j_*A$ whenever $A$ is quasi-coherent. For a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ in $\mathcal A_U$ and an affine open $V\subseteq X$, its inverse image $W=j^{-1}V$ is affine. The cokernel/image node applied to $A\to B$ gives $B(W)\twoheadrightarrow C(W)$ with kernel $A(W)$; here $C$ is its ambient cokernel by step 1. The section formula for pushforward therefore gives exactness after taking sections over each affine $V$, hence exactness as sheaves. Thus $j_*:\mathcal A_U\to\mathcal A_X$ is exact. By the exact-derived-functor node its total right derived functor $\Phi_j$ is the termwise functor on arbitrary complexes.

source.place: Tag 08D7, perfect-lemma-affine-pushforward: exactness from coherent.tex lemma-relative-affine-vanishing and derived.tex Tag 015F.

proof.text: Let $F$ be any integer-indexed complex in $\mathcal A_U$. Choose a functorial ambient K-injective resolution $s:F\to J$. The affine-pushforward resolution node gives that $j_*s:j_*F\to j_*J$ is a quasi-isomorphism, with no boundedness assumption. The left side represents $I_X\Phi_j(QF)$ by step 3 and the right side represents $Rj_*I_U(QF)$ by the definition of derived direct image. Thus the actual derived comparison is invertible: put $c_{QF}=Q(j_*s)\circ\varphi_F$ with $\varphi$ the termwise identification of step 3 (the inverse of the unit $\eta$); then $c\circ I_X(\eta)$ is the canonical map $Q(j_*F)\to Rj_*(QF)$, as hypothesis (c) of the criterion requires. These are the natural comparison maps induced by the functorial resolution; their invertibility on complex representatives makes the comparison a natural isomorphism on the derived category. This verifies the whole functor comparison required for each affine open, rather than inferring it just from sheaf-level acyclicity.

source.place: Tag 08D7, compatibility square; unbounded affine resolution comparison from the existing 08C2/0AVW node.

proof.text: Apply the affine-open criterion to $X$: quasi-compactness is assumed, quasi-separatedness is step 2, hypotheses (a) and (b) for every affine open are step 3 (quasi-coherence of $j_*$ and the termwise derived functor $\Phi_j$ with invertible unit), and hypothesis (c) is step 4. Consequently $I_X$ is an equivalence. Given $K$, choose $A\in D(\mathcal A_X)$ and an isomorphism $I_X(A)\simeq K$. Represent $A$ by an integer-indexed complex $F$ in $\mathcal A_X$, as in the derived-category construction. By the factorization in step 1 the underlying sheaf complex satisfies $Q(F)\simeq I_X(A)\simeq K$. Its terms are quasi-coherent by membership in $\mathcal A_X$. Every construction used the unbounded derived categories, so neither $K$ nor $F$ acquires a boundedness condition.
